name: Bullish flag
provenance_convention: Everything under book_facts is literal from the source (numbers unmodified). Everything under operational is a calibration or tooling choice; where a value is derived from a book statistic, the derivation is stated. Fields absent from the book are null.

units.days: as published in source; source does not state trading vs calendar days (one figure caption uses trading days). Bar conversions assume daily trading bars.
units.move_pct: percent price change per measurement_basis below

measurement_basis.description: Performance is measured from the start of the price trend preceding the flag (nearest minor low, for up breakouts) to the trend end after it — NOT breakout-to-ultimate-high (20% trend change) used for most patterns in the same source.
measurement_basis.not_comparable_to: all other pattern statistics; do not rank flags against other patterns on avg_move_pct

book_facts.description: A short sloping rectangle bounded by two parallel trend lines, appearing near the midpoint of a steep, quick price trend (a 'half-staff' pattern). Price usually consolidates against the prevailing trend, then breaks out upward and the prior advance resumes. Short-term bullish continuation. Study counted continuations only; reversals were excluded by design.

prior_trend.notes: 'Steep, quick price trend... prices rise or fall quickly, moving several points in just a few days to a few weeks.' No numeric minimum given. 'If you do not have a strong advance or decline leading to the chart pattern, ignore the flag.' Move measured trend-start low to flag high.

consolidation.slope_exceptions: Usually slopes against the trend; horizontal or upward slope also occurs ('exceptions are common').
consolidation.max_bars_note: Converts the stated 3-week maximum (an 'arbitrary limit') to daily trading bars. Formations longer than 3 weeks are better classified as symmetrical triangles, rectangles, or wedges.
consolidation.position_in_move: Usually near the midpoint of the move ('half-staff').

volume.during_flag_note: 'The volume trend nearly always recedes over the course of the formation' — not an inviolate rule.

breakout.definition: A breakout occurs when price closes outside the flag trend line.

performance.note: Bull flag = flag in an upward price trend (up breakout). Down-breakout columns in the source describe flags in downtrends and belong to a separate flag_bear spec.

busted_pattern_performance_pct.note: Fewer than 4 samples; author says ignore.

measured_move.notes: Difference between the start of the trend and the formation, projected above the end of the formation. A minimum move, met well below the 80% the author likes to see — set targets conservatively and be ready to close early.

trading_tactics.entry: Wait for breakout: take a position once price closes outside (above) the upper flag trend line. Formation end to breakout averages 2 days.
trading_tactics.stop_loss: No explicit rule for flags. Risk is sized to the nearest support/resistance level; in the worked example the stop sits slightly beyond the first such level. Compare measure-rule reward against distance to first/second support or resistance.
trading_tactics.exit: Take profits quickly: average 17 days to trend end; 58% of runs end within 2 weeks, 80% within a month (bull market). 'Flags are for swing traders.'

disqualifiers: No steep, quick price trend leading to the pattern ('ignore the flag')
Consolidation longer than 3 weeks — better classified as a symmetrical triangle, rectangle, or wedge; trade carefully or pass entirely
Flag not proportional to the move preceding it (failure example: 26-day flag after a short rise) — suggests impending failure or weak move
Nearby overhead resistance — throwbacks (43% of cases, bull market) cut the average rise from 31% to 13%

differential_diagnosis.distinction: Trendlines converge to a point; flag trendlines are parallel. Same measurement basis (only pattern statistically comparable to flags).

Preceded by a ~doubling of price. Separate pattern with far stronger statistics (avg rise 69% bull market, 0% break-even failure, rank 1). If the pole roughly doubles the price, classify as high-and-tight instead.
Same general shapes but duration over 3 weeks.
Horizontal parallel boundaries, longer duration, not embedded mid steep trend.

known_failure_modes: Excessive length (>3 weeks) and/or short prior rise — pattern completes but price fails to continue
Measure-rule shortfall: post-flag run shorter than pre-flag run; support/resistance beneath or above the flag truncates the move
Throwback to breakout price (43% bull market; returns in ~14 days) followed by weak continuation

operational.agent_prompt: You detect bullish flag patterns on daily stock charts. STRUCTURE — three parts: (1) POLE: a steep, fast advance, price moving up several percent in a few days to a few weeks (typical: ~22% over ~15 trading days). A gradual or meandering rise disqualifies the setup; skip it. (2) FLAG: a brief consolidation of a few days to 3 weeks maximum (typical 8-10 daily bars), price bounded by two roughly PARALLEL trendlines, usually drifting down against the trend (horizontal or slightly upward drift is acceptable), typical channel height ~7% of price, sitting near the midpoint of the overall move. Volume should recede through the consolidation. (3) BREAKOUT: a daily close above the upper trendline, typically within ~2 days of the flag ending. Strong breakout volume is NOT required — light-volume breakouts have performed slightly better (avg +26% vs +19%). REJECT when: trendlines converge (that is a pennant); consolidation exceeds 3 weeks (triangle/rectangle/wedge territory); the pole is weak or absent; the flag is disproportionately large versus the pole; or the advance leading in roughly doubled the price (that is a high-and-tight flag — a different, stronger pattern). EXPECTATIONS (daily US stocks, bull market, n=149; moves measured from trend start to trend end, so not comparable to other pattern types): average total move +23%; 4% of patterns fail to gain even 5%, but 20% fail to reach +10% and 36% fail to reach +15%; 64% reach the measured target; a throwback to the breakout price occurs 43% of the time and cuts the average move to +13% (vs +31% without). PRICE TARGET (minimum): flag_end_low + (flag_start_high - trend_start_low). TIMING: average 17 days from breakout to trend end; 58% of runs finish within 2 weeks and 80% within a month — this is a swing trade; take profits quickly. RANK candidates higher when: channel height above ~6.7% of price AND length above ~8 bars (tall+wide averaged +36%); flag volume trend falling; breakout volume light; breakout within the top third of the 52-week range (+26% avg); no significant overhead resistance nearby (throwback risk). In bear markets the same setup averaged only +17% (n=133) — favor bull-market conditions.

image_library.purpose: Labeled reference images for the pattern-matching agent, manually recreated from the source book's figures. Filenames are source-anchored (chapter name + chapter_figure); pattern classification and role live in this manifest, not in the filename.
image_library.missing_file_policy: Entries with optional=true are skipped silently if the file does not exist. Only optional=false entries may raise a missing-file error.

images.note: Figure contains two flags. The bull flag is the SECOND one (after price turns up at the bottom). The first is a bear flag — within this same image it doubles as a wrong-trend negative.
26-day flag after a short prior rise; price failed to continue. Teaches the >3-week and pole-proportionality disqualifiers.

negative_references.note: Bear flag: upward-sloping channel in a downtrend — must NOT match as bull flag.
Bear flag midway in a downtrend.
Bear flag; also illustrates the measure-rule shortfall.
Bear flag; the book's measure-rule worked example.

cross_references.flag_bear: The negative_references files are flag_bear's positive exemplars — same PNGs, dual role; chapter-based naming means no renaming or duplication.
cross_references.near_miss_negatives: Recreations of figures from the Pennants, Wedges (rising/falling), and Symmetrical Triangles chapters double as same-trend near-miss negatives for this pattern.

coverage_gaps: No same-trend near-miss negatives yet (pennant/wedge/>3-week channel in an uptrend) — pending recreation of sibling chapters
No throwback example (occurs in 43% of bull-market cases)
Single clean positive exemplar; style diversity (candles vs bars, log vs linear) not represented
